The merged fit of the drift diffusion model (`analysis/models/ddm5.rds`) at the participant level: each
participant's own indices, how they hang together across illusions, and how
much of the group differences age, language, student status and the
questionnaires account for, and whether, among users, the indices follow the
time since the last use or the lifetime number of uses. The population-level group differences are in
`3_ddm_groups.qmd`; the indices are defined in `analysis/server/marginals.R`.
Render from the repo root (about 2 min):

```bash
quarto render analysis/4_ddm_correlates.qmd
```

Two caveats apply to everything below.

- **Shrinkage.** The participant estimates are shrunk towards their group's
  mean, since Group is in the model. That flattens every within-group slope,
  so what a covariate accounts for is understated. Adjusting properly needs a
  refit with the covariate in the model. The same regressions on raw summaries
  of the trials, which are not shrunk, are the check.
- **Exploratory.** Several indices, three illusions and eight covariates make
  many cells. The illusion magnitude is the primary index; everything else is
  descriptive.

Every index is taken at mid task difficulty (`Task_Difficulty = 0`) and, for
the correlates, averaged over the three illusions per posterior draw.

## Loading

```{r}
library(brms)
library(ggplot2)

# Runs from analysis/ (quarto) or from the repo root (interactively).
root <- if (dir.exists("server")) "." else "analysis"
source(file.path(root, "server/models.R"))
source(file.path(root, "server/marginals.R"))

stopifnot(utils::packageVersion("cogmod") >= "0.3.6")
fit_file <- Sys.getenv("IGSA_FIT", unset = file.path(root, "models/ddm5.rds"))
out_dir <- file.path(root, "results")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

m <- readRDS(fit_file)
participants <- read.csv(file.path(root, "../data/open/participants.csv"))
q_file <- file.path(root, "../data/questionnaires.csv")
if (!file.exists(q_file)) stop(q_file, " not found: render analysis/0_preprocessing.qmd first", call. = FALSE)
questionnaires <- read.csv(q_file)
# Days since the last classic psychedelic and the lifetime number of uses.
groups <- read.csv(file.path(root, "../data/groups.csv"))

group_col <- c(Never = "#7a7a75", Past = "#2a78d6", Recent = "#eb6834")
contrast_col <- c("Past - Never" = "#2a78d6", "Recent - Never" = "#eb6834",
                  "Recent - Past" = "#1baf7a")
illusions <- c(Ebbinghaus = "Ebbinghaus", MullerLyer = "Müller-Lyer",
               VerticalHorizontal = "Vertical-Horizontal")
theme_igsa <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#ebebe8", linewidth = 0.3),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#6b6b66", hjust = 0)
  )
```

## Participant indices

Per participant and illusion, from 1,000 evenly spaced draws with the
participant's random effects in:

- With no illusion: discriminability (the drift towards the correct response), the boundary separation,
  non-decision time and P(error).
- The effect of the illusion, from strength 0 to 1: on discriminability and on
  P(error).
- Precision: the change in discriminability from mid difficulty to the hardest
  trials (negative: harder trials lower it).
- **Illusion magnitude**: the illusion effect on discriminability over the
  precision term. Both are negative, so it is positive: how many units of
  `Task_Difficulty` one unit of `Illusion_Strength` costs. It is the PSE shift
  in stimulus units, and it is unchanged by anything that scales the whole
  surface (`marginals.R`, `igsa_index()`).

```{r}
draw_ids <- round(seq(1, ndraws(m), length.out = 1000))
pg <- igsa_participant_grid(m, strength = c(0, 1), difficulty = c(0, 1))
pd <- igsa_draws(m, pg, re_formula = NULL, draw_ids = draw_ids)
pd$poutlier <- NULL

# One canonical order of participant x illusion cells; every matrix below is
# aligned to it by key.
cells <- unique(pg[c("Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type")])
cells <- cells[order(cells$Participant, cells$Illusion_Type), ]
rownames(cells) <- NULL
cell_key <- paste(cells$Participant, cells$Illusion_Type)
align <- function(x, grid) x[, match(cell_key, paste(grid$Participant, grid$Illusion_Type)), drop = FALSE]

at00 <- pg$Illusion_Strength == 0 & pg$Task_Difficulty == 0
base <- lapply(pd, function(x) align(x[, at00, drop = FALSE], pg[at00, ]))
ix <- igsa_index(pd, pg)
ix <- lapply(ix, align, grid = attr(ix, "grid"))
eff <- igsa_slopes(pd, pg, from = 0, to = 1)
eff_grid <- attr(eff, "grid")
eff <- lapply(eff, function(x) align(x[, eff_grid$Task_Difficulty == 0, drop = FALSE],
                                     eff_grid[eff_grid$Task_Difficulty == 0, ]))

quantities <- list(
  "Discriminability, no illusion" = base$delta,
  "Boundary, no illusion" = base$boundary,
  "Non-decision time (s), no illusion" = base$ndt,
  "P(error), no illusion" = base$perror,
  "Illusion effect on discriminability" = ix$delta_strength,
  "Illusion effect on P(error)" = eff$perror,
  "Precision (difficulty slope)" = ix$delta_difficulty,
  "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)" = ix$index
)
primary <- "Illusion magnitude (strength / difficulty)"

# Averaged over the three illusions, per draw: draws x participants.
per_participant <- function(x) {
  idx <- split(seq_len(nrow(cells)), factor(cells$Participant, levels = unique(cells$Participant)))
  sapply(idx, function(i) rowMeans(x[, i, drop = FALSE]))
}
avg <- lapply(quantities, per_participant)
ids <- colnames(avg[[1]])
```

The ratio is unstable wherever the precision term crosses zero. The share of
draws in which it is non-negative, per participant and illusion:

```{r}
nonneg <- colMeans(ix$delta_difficulty >= 0)
unstable <- cells[nonneg > 0.05, ]
unstable$Share <- round(nonneg[nonneg > 0.05], 2)
```

`r nrow(unstable)` of `r nrow(cells)` participant × illusion cells have more
than 5% of their draws with a non-negative precision term (maximum share
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(nonneg))`). The index is summarised by its posterior
median throughout, which is robust to a few such draws.

```{r}
if (nrow(unstable)) knitr::kable(unstable, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# Per participant x illusion, and averaged ("All"), with the covariates.
summarise_cells <- function(x, grid) {
  data.frame(grid, Median = apply(x, 2, stats::median),
             CI_low = apply(x, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025),
             CI_high = apply(x, 2, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975), row.names = NULL)
}
ppt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(quantities), function(qn) {
  rbind(
    cbind(Quantity = qn, summarise_cells(quantities[[qn]], cells)),
    cbind(Quantity = qn, summarise_cells(avg[[qn]], data.frame(
      Participant = ids, Group = cells$Group[match(ids, cells$Participant)], Illusion_Type = "All")))
  )
}))
info <- data.frame(Participant = ids, Group = factor(cells$Group[match(ids, cells$Participant)],
                                                     levels = names(group_col)))
info <- merge(info, participants[c("Participant", "Age", "Language_Level", "Student")], sort = FALSE)
info <- merge(info, questionnaires[c("Participant", "AAQ", "DASS_Total", "MEQ_Total", "MEQ_Mystical",
                                     "MEQ_PositiveMood", "MEQ_Transcendence", "MEQ_Ineffability")], sort = FALSE)
info <- merge(info, groups[c("Participant", "Days", "Psychedelics_Frequency")], all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
info <- info[match(ids, info$Participant), ]
info$Native <- as.integer(info$Language_Level == "Native")
info$Student <- as.integer(info$Student == "Yes")
# Lifetime use was a choice among these categories (experiment/demographics.js),
# scored 1 to 6. "Never" (one user, who described a last experience with
# ayahuasca) and the naive group are missing.
lifetime_levels <- c("One time", "Between 2 and 5 times", "Between 6 and 10 times", "Between 11 and 50 times",
                     "Between 51 and 100 times", "More than 100 times")
stopifnot(info$Psychedelics_Frequency %in% c(lifetime_levels, "Never", NA))
info$Lifetime <- as.integer(factor(info$Psychedelics_Frequency, levels = lifetime_levels))
info$Days[info$Group == "Never"] <- NA
write.csv(merge(ppt, info[c("Participant", "Age", "Native", "Student", "AAQ", "DASS_Total", "MEQ_Total", "Days", "Lifetime")]),
          file.path(out_dir, "ddm_participants.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

The medians per participant and illusion are in
`analysis/results/ddm_participants.csv`, with age and the questionnaire
scores. Their distribution per group:

```{r}

ppt$Quantity <- factor(ppt$Quantity, levels = names(quantities))
ppt$Illusion <- factor(c(illusions, All = "All (averaged)")[ppt$Illusion_Type],
                       levels = c(illusions, "All (averaged)"))
ppt$Group <- factor(ppt$Group, levels = names(group_col))

ggplot(ppt, aes(Median, Group, colour = Group)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.15, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0, alpha = 0.5, size = 0.9) +

  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(x = "Participant posterior median", y = NULL,
       title = "Participant indices per group",
       caption = "Mid task difficulty. Each point is one participant's posterior median. Each panel has its own x scale.") +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 7))
```

## Across illusions

Is there one illusion sensitivity? The correlation across participants
between each pair of illusions, per posterior draw, for the main indices:

```{r}
cor_pairs <- function(Q) {
  ill <- levels(droplevels(cells$Illusion_Type))
  pairs <- utils::combn(ill, 2)
  do.call(rbind, apply(pairs, 2, function(p) {
    a <- Q[, cells$Illusion_Type == p[1], drop = FALSE]
    b <- Q[, cells$Illusion_Type == p[2], drop = FALSE]
    r <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(Q)), function(i) stats::cor(a[i, ], b[i, ]), numeric(1))
    data.frame(Pair = paste(illusions[p[1]], "&", illusions[p[2]]), Median = stats::median(r),
               CI_low = stats::quantile(r, 0.025), CI_high = stats::quantile(r, 0.975),
               pd = max(mean(r > 0), mean(r < 0)), row.names = NULL)
  }, simplify = FALSE))
}
cors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(primary, "Illusion effect on discriminability", "Illusion effect on P(error)",
                                "Precision (difficulty slope)", "Discriminability, no illusion"),
                              function(qn) cbind(Quantity = qn, cor_pairs(quantities[[qn]]))))
write.csv(cors, file.path(out_dir, "ddm_correlations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(cors, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.4

med <- ppt[ppt$Quantity == primary & ppt$Illusion_Type != "All", c("Participant", "Group", "Illusion_Type", "Median")]
wide <- stats::reshape(med, idvar = c("Participant", "Group"), timevar = "Illusion_Type", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^Median\\.", "", names(wide))
pairs <- utils::combn(names(illusions), 2)
scatter <- do.call(rbind, apply(pairs, 2, function(p) {
  data.frame(Group = wide$Group, Pair = paste(illusions[p[1]], "vs", illusions[p[2]]),
             x = wide[[p[1]]], y = wide[[p[2]]])
}, simplify = FALSE))

ggplot(scatter, aes(x, y, colour = Group)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ Pair, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_col) +
  labs(x = "Illusion magnitude, first illusion", y = "Second illusion", colour = NULL,
       title = "Illusion magnitude across illusions",
       caption = "Participant posterior medians. The line is identity.") +
  theme_igsa
```

## What the covariates account for

Each participant's index, averaged over the illusions, is regressed on Group
alone, then on Group and a covariate, once per posterior draw. Each draw's
coefficients are themselves drawn from their sampling distribution, so the
intervals carry both the uncertainty of the participant estimates and that of
a regression on about a hundred people. Age is per 10 years; the questionnaire
scores are per standard deviation across the analysed participants. The MEQ-30
exists for users only, so its regressions compare Recent with Past.

Two more regressions, on users only, ask whether the indices follow psychedelic
use by degree, which the Recent / Past split at 30 days cannot show:

- **Days since the last use**, on a log scale (per tenfold increase: 3 days to
  30, or one month to ten), alone and with age. Group is left out of these two,
  since it is the same variable cut in two. Three past users gave no number of
  days and are out.
- **Lifetime use**, the six answer categories scored 1 to 6 (per category),
  with Group.

The raw summaries of the trials, regressed the same way, are the unshrunk
check: the 10th percentile of correct RTs (the fast tail, which tracks
non-decision time), and the error rates on facilitating-or-no-illusion and on
conflicting trials.

```{r}
trials <- m$data
correct <- trials[trials$Error == 0, ]
raw <- list(
  "Raw: fastest correct RTs (10th percentile, s)" = tapply(correct$RT, correct$Participant, stats::quantile, probs = 0.1),
  "Raw: error rate, facilitating or no illusion" = with(trials[trials$Illusion_Strength <= 0, ], tapply(Error, Participant, mean)),
  "Raw: error rate, conflicting illusion" = with(trials[trials$Illusion_Strength > 0, ], tapply(Error, Participant, mean))
)
raw <- lapply(raw, function(x) matrix(x[ids], nrow = length(draw_ids), ncol = length(ids),
                                      byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, ids)))
outcomes <- c(avg, raw)

z <- function(x) (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / stats::sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
info$Age10 <- (info$Age - mean(info$Age, na.rm = TRUE)) / 10
info$LogDays <- log10(info$Days)
stopifnot(all(info$Days > 0, na.rm = TRUE))
for (s in c("AAQ", "DASS_Total", "MEQ_Total", "MEQ_Mystical", "MEQ_PositiveMood", "MEQ_Transcendence", "MEQ_Ineffability")) {
  info[[paste0(s, "_z")]] <- z(info[[s]])
}

designs <- list(
  "Group" = ~ Group,
  "Group + age" = ~ Group + Age10,
  "Group + age + native + student" = ~ Group + Age10 + Native + Student,
  "Group + AAQ-II" = ~ Group + AAQ_z,
  "Group + DASS-21" = ~ Group + DASS_Total_z,
  "Group + MEQ-30 total (users)" = ~ Group + MEQ_Total_z,
  "Group + MEQ mystical (users)" = ~ Group + MEQ_Mystical_z,
  "Group + MEQ positive mood (users)" = ~ Group + MEQ_PositiveMood_z,
  "Group + MEQ transcendence (users)" = ~ Group + MEQ_Transcendence_z,
  "Group + MEQ ineffability (users)" = ~ Group + MEQ_Ineffability_z,
  "Days since last use (users)" = ~ LogDays,
  "Days since last use + age (users)" = ~ LogDays + Age10,
  "Group + lifetime use (users)" = ~ Group + Lifetime
)
term_labels <- c(
  GroupPast = "Past - Never", GroupRecent = "Recent - Never", Age10 = "Age (per 10 years)",
  Native = "Native speaker", Student = "Student", AAQ_z = "AAQ-II (per SD)",
  DASS_Total_z = "DASS-21 (per SD)", MEQ_Total_z = "MEQ-30 total (per SD)",
  MEQ_Mystical_z = "MEQ mystical (per SD)", MEQ_PositiveMood_z = "MEQ positive mood (per SD)",
  MEQ_Transcendence_z = "MEQ transcendence (per SD)", MEQ_Ineffability_z = "MEQ ineffability (per SD)",
  LogDays = "Days since last use (per tenfold)", Lifetime = "Lifetime use (per category)"
)

# One coefficient vector per posterior draw, drawn from its sampling
# distribution around that draw's least-squares fit, on the complete cases
# of the design.
regress <- function(Q, formula) {
  vars <- all.vars(formula)
  keep <- stats::complete.cases(info[vars])
  d <- droplevels(info[keep, ])
  X <- stats::model.matrix(formula, d)
  Y <- t(Q[, keep, drop = FALSE])
  fit <- qr(X)
  B <- qr.coef(fit, Y)
  s2 <- colSums(qr.resid(fit, Y)^2) / (nrow(X) - ncol(X))
  L <- chol(solve(crossprod(X)))
  B <- B + t(L) %*% matrix(stats::rnorm(length(B)), nrow(B)) * rep(sqrt(s2), each = nrow(B))
  # Without Never (users only), Past is the reference.
  if (!"Never" %in% levels(d$Group)) rownames(B) <- sub("^GroupRecent$", "GroupRecentPast", rownames(B))
  list(B = B, n = nrow(X))
}
term_labels <- c(term_labels, GroupRecentPast = "Recent - Past")

set.seed(1)
coefs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(outcomes), function(qn) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(designs), function(k) {
    r <- regress(outcomes[[qn]], designs[[k]])
    do.call(rbind, lapply(intersect(names(term_labels), rownames(r$B)), function(tm) {
      v <- r$B[tm, ]
      data.frame(Quantity = qn, Design = k, N = r$n, Term = term_labels[[tm]], Median = stats::median(v),
                 CI_low = stats::quantile(v, 0.025), CI_high = stats::quantile(v, 0.975),
                 pd = max(mean(v > 0), mean(v < 0)), row.names = NULL)
    }))
  }))
}))
coefs$Quantity <- factor(coefs$Quantity, levels = names(outcomes))
coefs$Design <- factor(coefs$Design, levels = names(designs))
write.csv(coefs, file.path(out_dir, "ddm_correlates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### The group differences, unadjusted and adjusted

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 12

group_terms <- c("Past - Never", "Recent - Never", "Recent - Past")
adj <- coefs[coefs$Term %in% group_terms, ]
adj$Design <- factor(adj$Design, levels = rev(names(designs)))
adj$Term <- factor(adj$Term, levels = group_terms)

ggplot(adj, aes(Median, Design, colour = Term, group = Term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high), linewidth = 0.7,
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = Term), size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~ Quantity, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(40)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = contrast_col) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Past - Never" = 16, "Recent - Never" = 17, "Recent - Past" = 15)) +
  labs(x = "Difference between groups (median, 95% interval)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
       title = "Group differences, unadjusted and adjusted",
       caption = "Rows: what the participant estimates are regressed on. Indices averaged over the illusions.") +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 8))
```

### The covariates themselves

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 12

cov <- coefs[!coefs$Term %in% group_terms, ]
cov$Term <- factor(cov$Term, levels = rev(unique(term_labels[!term_labels %in% group_terms])))

ggplot(cov, aes(Median, Term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#9a9a95", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high), linewidth = 0.7, colour = "#2a78d6") +
  geom_point(size = 2, colour = "#2a78d6") +
  facet_wrap(~ Quantity, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2, labeller = label_wrap_gen(40)) +
  labs(x = "Coefficient, adjusted for Group (median, 95% interval)", y = NULL,
       title = "What each covariate adds, with Group in the regression",
       caption = "Age per 10 years; questionnaire scores per SD. MEQ-30, days since last use and lifetime use: users only.") +
  theme_igsa + theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 8))
```

```{r}
cov_tab <- cov[cov$Quantity %in% c(names(quantities), names(raw)), c("Quantity", "Term", "N", "Median", "CI_low", "CI_high", "pd")]
cov_tab$Value <- sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", cov_tab$Median, cov_tab$CI_low, cov_tab$CI_high)
wide <- stats::reshape(cov_tab[c("Quantity", "Term", "Value")], idvar = "Quantity", timevar = "Term", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^Value\\.", "", names(wide))
wide[is.na(wide)] <- ""
knitr::kable(wide, row.names = FALSE)
```

       title = "Participant indices against the time since the last use (users)",
       caption = "Posterior medians, averaged over the illusions. Line: a linear fit on log days. Dashed: the 30-day split between Recent and Past.") +
  theme_igsa
